gloss: to look back; to turn around and look; to get back at someone by proving oneself

definitions.gloss: to look back; to turn around and look
definitions.explanation: To turn one's head or body to look at something behind or beside oneself.

definitions.gloss: to get back at; to prove oneself; to show them
definitions.explanation: To succeed or achieve something impressive in order to prove wrong those who doubted, looked down on, or criticized you.

examples.japanese: {声|こえ}をかけられて{見返|みかえ}った。
examples.english: Someone called out to me, and I turned around to look.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}はちらっと{見返|みかえ}って{微笑|ほほえ}んだ。
{振|ふ}り{返|かえ}って{見返|みかえ}ると、{誰|だれ}もいなかった。
examples.english: When I turned around to look, no one was there.

examples.japanese: バカにした{人|ひと}たちを{見返|みかえ}してやる。
examples.english: I'll show those people who made fun of me.

examples.japanese: {努力|どりょく}して{周|まわ}りを{見返|みかえ}したい。
examples.english: I want to work hard and prove everyone wrong.

examples.japanese: {失敗|しっぱい}を{笑|わら}った{人|ひと}たちを{見返|みかえ}すために、{必死|ひっし}に{頑張|がんば}った。
examples.english: I worked desperately to prove wrong those who laughed at my failure.

notes:
An ichidan verb with two distinct meanings. Sense 1 is a simple physical action. Sense 2 carries strong emotional motivation — the desire to vindicate oneself and prove doubters wrong.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ～を{見返|みかえ}してやる: I'll show them! / I'll prove them wrong!
- {周|まわ}りを{見返|みかえ}す: to prove everyone around you wrong
- バカにした{人|ひと}を{見返|みかえ}す: to get back at people who looked down on you

SIMILAR WORDS (sense 1):
- {振|ふ}り{返|かえ}る: to turn around; to look back — more common for this physical meaning
- {振|ふ}り{向|む}く: to turn to face someone — implies facing toward

SIMILAR WORDS (sense 2):
- {見返|みかえ}す: to look back at — can also mean to get revenge/prove oneself (similar)
- {仕返|しかえ}しする: to get revenge — more direct retaliation
